note: Influence and approval are gameplay starting values for 1 January 2000 (Jiang Zemin and Zhu Rongji leadership), not measured data. Influence reflects institutional weight in a one-party state: the PLA and the security apparatus are answerable to the party and powerful within it; state-owned and private business gained weight under market reform; there are no independent unions (the All-China Federation of Trade Unions is party-led), no independent press and no legal opposition.

interest_groups.note: The PLA answers to the party Central Military Commission, which Jiang Zemin chaired.
Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of State Security and the People's Armed Police.
State-owned enterprises under restructuring alongside a growing private and foreign-invested sector.
Only the party-led ACFTU is legal. Approval is reduced by state-enterprise layoffs (xiagang) under the late-1990s reforms.
Officially registered religious associations under state supervision; unregistered groups operate outside the system.
